I read the test and the relevant part of `ConversationHandler.check_update`.

From the test setup, `conversation._conversations[key] = "ACTIVE"` before calling `conversation.check_update(update)`, so inside `check_update` the current `state` is not `None`. The code at lines 766–776 only searches entry points if `state is None or self.allow_reentry`. For this test, the important branch is the next one: lines 778–783 iterate over `self.states.get(state, [])` because `state` is set and no handler has been found yet.

The test defines `states={"ACTIVE": state_handlers}` and `state_handlers` is a list of 9 handlers, in this order:
1. `ChatMemberHandler`
2. `BusinessConnectionHandler`
3. `CommandHandler`
4. `PrefixHandler`
5. `MessageHandler(filters.CaptionRegex(...))`
6. `MessageHandler(filters.TEXT & filters.Regex(theta) & filters.Entity(URL))`
7. `MessageHandler((filters.TEXT & filters.Regex(alpha)) & filters.FORWARDED)`
8. `MessageHandler(filters.TEXT & (~filters.COMMAND) & (filters.Regex(beta) | filters.Regex(gamma)))`
9. `MessageHandler(filters.ALL)`

The loop stops at the first candidate whose `check_update(update)` is neither `None` nor `False` (lines 780–783). For the concrete update in the test:
- it is a normal text message, not a chat member update, not a business connection update, and not a command/prefix command;
- it has text `"alpha beta gamma theta"`;
- it has a bold entity, not a URL entity;
- nothing in the test marks it as forwarded;
- therefore the first 7 candidates do not satisfy their filters;
- candidate 8 does satisfy `filters.TEXT`, `~filters.COMMAND`, and the regex alternative `(beta | gamma)` because the text contains both words.

So the loop reaches candidate 8 and breaks there. That means it executes 8 iterations total.
